extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying, making, and overcoming statutory and nonstatutory double patenting rejections (including form paragraphs, examiner procedures, terminal disclaimers, and interactions with prior art rejections and 35 U.S.C. 121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental reason for rule against double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental reason for the rule is to prevent unjustified timewise extension of the right to exclude granted by a patent no matter how the extension is brought about; to prevail the appellant has the burden of establishing that the invention claimed is 'independent and distinct' from the invention of the appealed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting In re Schneller: where allowance of appealed claims would extend patent protection already disclosed and covered by claims of the patent, and there is no terminal disclaimer or mitigating circumstances, the rule against double patenting must be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schneller-based nonstatutory double patenting is limited and requires approval
rubrics_metrics.description: In re Schneller did not establish a rule of general application and is limited to particular facts; nonstatutory double patenting rejections based on Schneller will be rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Technology Center (TC) Director must approve any nonstatutory double patenting rejections based on Schneller. Examiner should first consult SPE; if SPE agrees, obtain TC Director approval before making such a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph sequencing and mandatory use of form 8.33
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 8.33 must precede any one of form paragraphs 8.34 to 8.39 and must be used only ONCE in an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form paragraph (8.38 or 8.39 etc.) after 8.33. Follow bracket insertion guidance (insert patent or application numbers, description of subject matter) and examiner notes concerning when each form paragraph is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶8.38 Double Patenting - Nonstatutory (With a Patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected on ground of nonstatutory double patenting over claim [2] of U.S. Patent No. [3] since the claims, if allowed, would improperly extend the 'right to exclude' already granted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only where subject matter of the application is fully disclosed in, and covered by at least one claim of, an issued U.S. Patent which is commonly owned or where there is common inventorship. Obtain TC Director approval for Schneller-based rejections. If conflicting patent is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g), make additional 102/103 rejections as appropriate (form paragraph 7.21). For patents to another inventive entity and earlier filing date, consider 102(e)/103(a) rejection using form paragraph 7.21.02, subject to 103(c) disqualification rules for applications pending on/after Dec 10, 2004.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶8.39 Double Patenting - Nonstatutory (With Another Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] provisionally rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting over claim [2] of copending Application No. [3]. This is a provisional double patenting rejection because the conflicting claims have not in fact been patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only where subject matter is fully disclosed in and covered by at least one claim of another copending application which is commonly owned or where there is common inventorship. Obtain TC Director approval for Schneller-based rejections. Make provisional double patenting rejection in the other application as well. If evidence shows prior art issues under 102(f)/(g), make additional 102/103 rejections as appropriate (form paragraph 7.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Each double patenting situation decided on its own facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting determinations are fact-specific; courts and MPEP stress individualized analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider inventorship, filing history, disclosures in the patents/applications, and statutory changes (e.g., pre- vs post-1984 joint inventorship rules) when evaluating whether a double patenting rejection is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design/Plant vs Utility double patenting principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting principles and criteria applied in utility-utility situations generally apply to utility-plant or utility-design situations; double patenting may be raised where applicant filed both utility and plant or design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting may be found in design-utility situations irrespective of whether claims involve the same invention or obvious variations. Some cases suggest a two-way obviousness determination is necessary in design-utility cases (Carman Indus.); examine claim scopes (interior construction vs external configuration) and whether they are obvious variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between double patenting rejection and 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) prior art rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A double patenting rejection must rely on comparison with the claims in an issued or to be issued patent, whereas a 102(e)/103(a) rejection relies on what is disclosed (whether or not claimed) in the same issued or to be issued patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer cannot obviate a 102(e)/103(a) rejection. For applications pending on or after Nov 29, 1999 and on/after Dec 10, 2004, commonly assigned/owned patents/applications may be disqualified as 102(e) prior art under 103(c)(1). Examiners should make both 102(e)/103 and double patenting rejections when facts support both; omission of one when applicable prevents making next Office action final if the omitted rejection is added later.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use form paragraph 8.28 (priority/102(f)/(g) issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conflicting application is currently commonly assigned but the file does not establish common ownership at the time the later invention was made, form paragraph 8.28 may be used in addition to the nonstatutory double patenting paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.28 to address priority and potential 35 U.S.C. 102(f)/(g) issues when ownership/timing facts are unclear. Consider additional 102/103 rejections in the other application as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding statutory double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory double patenting rejection can be avoided by amending the conflicting claims so that they are not coextensive in scope or by canceling the conflicting claims in the pending applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where conflicting claims are in multiple pending applications, cancel conflicting claims in all but one application to avoid provisional statutory rejections. A terminal disclaimer is not effective against statutory double patenting. Use of a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit to overcome statutory double patenting is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding nonstatutory double patenting rejections (terminal disclaimer)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on a nonstatutory type of double patenting can be avoided by filing a terminal disclaimer in the application or proceeding in which the rejection is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer practice supported by case law (In re Vogel, Knohl, Griswold, Jentoft, Eckel, Braithwaite). Terminal disclaimers encourage disclosure and earlier expiration of patents. Filing a terminal disclaimer is not an admission of the propriety of the rejection. For commonly owned subject matter, the disclaimer must include a provision that the patent shall be unenforceable if it ceases to be commonly owned (37 CFR 1.321(c)). 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits are inapplicable where claims are directed to substantially the same invention or lack patentable distinctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer mechanics and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer is a statement filed by an owner to disclaim or dedicate a portion of the entire term of all the claims of a patent; requirements are set forth in 37 CFR 1.321 and sample forms/guidance in MPEP §1490.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terminal disclaimer must operate with respect to all claims in the patent; statute does not provide for disclaimer of only specified claim(s). When the claimed invention resulted from a joint research agreement, 37 CFR 1.321(d) sets forth additional requirements. A terminal disclaimer must include commonly-owned provisions when required and may need to extend to continuing applications by its terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer required for nonstatutory double patenting in applications filed on/after June 8, 1995
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuing utility or plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 (20-year term regime), a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321 is required to overcome a nonstatutory double patenting rejection, even if the application claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2) sets 20-year patent term rules and 154(b) allows for patent term extensions; 37 CFR 1.321(c)(3) prevents harassment by multiple parties by requiring common ownership provisions. Examiners should cite this MPEP section or Official Gazette notice when applicants argue a terminal disclaimer should not be required due to 35 U.S.C. 154 change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition against double patenting does not apply (exceptions A–G)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibits use of a patent issued on an application that was subject to an Office restriction requirement as a reference against a divisional filed before the patent issues, but this prohibition has exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: (A) applicant voluntarily filed divisional without restriction requirement; (B) claims not consonant with restriction requirement because materially changed; (C) restriction was made subject to nonallowance of generic/linking claims and such claims were subsequently allowed (requirement must be withdrawn); (D) restriction made only in an international application by ISA/IPEA; (E) restriction withdrawn by examiner before patent issues; (F) claims in second application are drawn to 'same invention' as first application (studiengesellschaft); (G) requirement for restriction between product/process/use made subject to nonallowance of product and product is later allowed (requirement must be withdrawn). Maintain consonance of line of demarcation to preserve protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple conflicting double patenting references and terminal disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple conflicting patents and/or pending applications are applied in double patenting rejections in a single application, a terminal disclaimer(s) must be filed to disclaim patent term that would extend beyond each conflicting patent/application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer fee is required for each terminal disclaimer filed. To avoid multiple fees, a single terminal disclaimer based on common ownership may be filed that bases the term disclaimed on all conflicting commonly owned references; however, each commonly owned conflicting reference must be included in the terminal disclaimer to avoid future dual ownership problems. For joint research agreements, 37 CFR 1.321(d) applies.
